post.summary:
Email a sign-in code: the first step of creating an account and of
signing in with a code (D-59, D-60). Sending again is the same call.
The answer is the same for any address, with an account or not.

Sign in with the emailed code, making the account if the address has
none. Sets the refresh cookie. `account.completed` false: the account
must be completed before anything else (D-61).
Sign in. Sets the refresh cookie.
A new access token, from the refresh cookie. Replaces the cookie too: each is used once.
End this session. Always succeeds, and clears the cookie.

The "complete your account" step (D-61): the only way an account made
by a code or by Google gets past ACCOUNT_INCOMPLETE. The access token in
use keeps working; read `GET /users/me` again for the profile.

post.summary: Email a code for choosing a new password. The answer is the same for any address.

Choose a new password with the emailed code. Ends every earlier session,
then signs in here: sets a new refresh cookie.
Change the password, knowing the current one. Ends every other session.

Ask to delete your own account, with the password as proof it is you.
It is deleted 14 days later unless you sign in and restore it (D-141).
Every session ends, this one included; the owner is emailed the date.

Restore an account waiting to be deleted: for the dialog shown after
signing in to one. The only route such an account may use besides
`GET /users/me`. Restoring one that is not waiting changes nothing.

`/auth/callback?error=cancelled|failed|email_unverified|account_deleted`.

Also before the account is completed, and while it waits to be deleted:
the client reads `completed` and `deletes_at` to know where to go.

A form to upload one file for a channel, valid 15 minutes. Needs

name's extension must be of a type sent (UPLOAD_INVALID_TYPE, D-92,
D-177), the size at most 25 MB (UPLOAD_FILE_TOO_LARGE). At most 60
forms a minute per person (RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, with Retry-After).

says: the file is deleted (UPLOAD_INVALID_TYPE). Nothing uploaded yet:
UPLOAD_FILE_NOT_FOUND. Done once, it answers the same again.

author.description: Null once that message is deleted.

edited_at.description: Shown as "edited"; null if never edited.

person, <@&id> a role, <#id> a channel, and @everyone (REQ-MSG-03).

mention_roles.description: The roles it mentions in effect, as named now; a role deleted since is left out (D-171).

Whom a system message is about (`{ user_id }`, `{ user_id, message_id }`,
D-168); a task's reminder: `{ task_id, title, reminder, due_at, user_ids }`,
its title when sent. Null on a regular one.

system_user.description: That person, named and pictured like an author; null on a regular message, or one naming no one.

system_users.description: The people a task's reminder is for, in order, named like authors (D-95, D-182); empty on any other message.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers; null if none (REQ-MSG-05).

edited_at.description: Shown as "edited"; null if never edited.

attachments.description: Its files, in the order sent (REQ-MSG-04): images first is the client's to draw (C-10).

content.description:
Plain text; empty on a system message. Mentions are tokens: <@id> a
person, <@&id> a role, <#id> a channel, and @everyone (REQ-MSG-03).

mention_everyone.description: @everyone in effect: the author had MENTION_EVERYONE. Otherwise the words are only words.

content.description: At most 2000 characters, an emoji counting as one, once the blank around it is dropped; empty only with files.

nonce.description:
Chosen by the client for this message and kept across its retries: the
same nonce again answers with the message already sent (REQ-MSG-10),
and `message.created` carries it back so the sender's "sending" copy
is swapped for the saved one.

reply_to_id.description: The message this one answers: a regular message of the same channel, deleted or not (REQ-MSG-05).

attachment_ids.description:
Checked uploads of the sender's (`POST /attachments/{id}/complete`), in
the order they show: at most 10, each once (REQ-MSG-04). One that cannot
be sent (not checked, sent already, older than 24 hours) is named in
UPLOAD_FILE_NOT_FOUND's `attachment_ids`.

content.description: 1-2000 characters, an emoji counting as one, once the blank around it is dropped.

type.description: `system`: made by the app (REQ-MSG-08), with no author.

mention_here_user_ids.description: Whom @here reached as it was sent (D-166): those not offline who saw the channel. The client marks it for them.

mention_users.description: The people its <@id> tokens name, as they are now (D-171); an id of no account is left out.

mention_roles.description: The roles it mentions in effect, as named now; a role deleted since is left out (D-171).

system_event.description: What a system message reports (`member_joined`, `message_pinned`, `task_due`); null on a regular one.

system_data.description:
Whom a system message is about (`{ user_id }`, `{ user_id, message_id }`,
D-168); a task's reminder: `{ task_id, title, reminder, due_at, user_ids }`,
its title when sent. Null on a regular one.

system_user.description: That person, named and pictured like an author; null on a regular message, or one naming no one.

system_users.description: The people a task's reminder is for, in order, named like authors (D-95, D-182); empty on any other message.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers; null if none (REQ-MSG-05).

edited_at.description: Shown as "edited"; null if never edited.

attachments.description: Its files, in the order sent (REQ-MSG-04): images first is the client's to draw (C-10).

content.description:
Plain text; empty on a system message. Mentions are tokens: <@id> a
person, <@&id> a role, <#id> a channel, and @everyone (REQ-MSG-03).

mention_everyone.description: @everyone in effect: the author had MENTION_EVERYONE. Otherwise the words are only words.

last_read_id.description:
The last message read: an id to compare others with, or to open the
channel around (`around`); maybe of a deleted message, or no message at
all when the reader never marked the channel and stands where they
joined the server (D-170).

unread_count.description: Live messages after it not sent by the reader, counted up to 100 (D-173): over 99 shows as "99+".

mention_count.description: Those of them about the reader (D-39, D-164, D-172), counted up to 100.

message_id.description:
The newest message of the channel the reader has seen (D-46), deleted
or not. Left out: the channel's newest message ("Mark as read"). The
mark only moves forward (D-173).

expires_at.description: The form is refused after this (15 minutes): ask for another.

channel_id.description: The channel the file is for: sending files there needs ATTACH_FILES (REQ-ROLE-03).

filename.description:
The file's name; its extension says its type (D-92, D-177). Kept without
folders or control characters, at most 255 characters.

size.description: In bytes: at most 25 MB (UPLOAD_FILE_TOO_LARGE), which the storage keeps too.

views_channel.description: False: still on the task but no longer views its channel ("Mất quyền xem kênh", D-194).

left_server.description: No longer a member of the task's server: "(đã rời server)", no presence (D-194).

completed_at.description: When it became done; null while it is not (ARCHITECTURE 7).

assignees.description: In the order they were given the task; none: "Chưa giao".

updated_at.description: Moves on every change: of two copies of a task, the client keeps the later one.

done_count.description: The "XONG — n" heading; null on a page of done tasks.

due_at.description: Later than now; null or left out: no due date.

assignee_ids.description: Members who view the channel; none: "Chưa giao".

completed_at.description: When it became done; null while it is not (ARCHITECTURE 7).

assignees.description: In the order they were given the task; none: "Chưa giao".

group.description:
Overdue, today, the next 7 days (tomorrow to today + 6), later, no due
date: counted in the time zone of one's settings when the list was read
(D-186). Null on a page of done tasks.

updated_at.description: Moves on every change: of two copies of a task, the client keeps the later one.

done_count.description: The "ĐÃ XONG — n" heading; null on a page of done tasks.

due_count.description: The tasks overdue or due today: the rail's "Việc" badge (C-05); null on a page of done tasks.

due_at.description: A new one must be later than now (D-96). Null: no due date.

user_ids.description: People already on it are skipped.

actor.description: Null when the app did it (an assignee who left the server).

subject.description: The person added or taken off; null for the other kinds.

from.description: Title, due date (an ISO time, null: none) or status before the change; null for the other kinds.

due_at.description: The due date then; null when it had none.

reminder.description: `task_reminder`: 24 hours or 2 hours before it is due (REQ-TASK-04); null on the other kinds.

unassigned_by.description:
`task_unassigned`: its last person took themselves off, or left the
server (D-95); `actor` is who. Null on the other kinds.

reason.description: A mention: by name, a role, @everyone or @here; null for a reply.

unread_count.description: Of the channels one views now, like the page.
